page: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the AWS Graviton processor family. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on the arm64 architecture, utilizing the AWS Neoverse-V3 CPU model running at 3.3 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It operates on the Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and has a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. There are no GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark results indicate strong memory and compression performance. The Passmark memory score is in the top tier, supported by a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 2282.43 GB/sec and a large-block write bandwidth of 78.36 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both achieve top-tier status, with gzip reaching 36.42 GB/sec. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is also strong at 257.5 GB/sec. For database operations, the instance registers a strong Passmark database score of 29240.13 and an average Redis SET performance of 48.47 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds are notable, with small model text generation reaching a top-tier 376.71 tokens/sec and medium model text generation achieving a strong 30.2 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ARMv9 architecture delivers high resource density and strong memory throughput relative to its general-purpose hardware class. The absence of local storage means users must rely on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff to consider. This instance is well-suited for workloads such as static web serving, database operations, medium-scale language model inference, and general-purpose application hosting.
